subject: NovaHealth order form — support & uptime redlines
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Hsu <mark.hsu@novahealth.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redlines on order form + uptime ask

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attached are the order form redlines from our procurement and legal teams (NovaOrderForm_Redlines_20261129.docx) plus a short summary of the high-level asks: 

- Uptime: asking to move from 99.9% to 99.95% for production cluster (reasoning: patient-facing integration).
- Service credits: higher step function if monthly uptime < 99.9%.
- Response times: P1 30 min acknowledgement, P2 4 hours, P3 24 hours.
- Maintenance windows: prefer scheduled maintenance limited to 02:00-05:00 US Eastern with 48-hour notice; blackout windows during clinical events (we'll provide dates).

We understand this may impact pricing — procurement asked for a clear tradeoff (credits or pricing adjustment). Can your team indicate what is negotiable vs. non-starter so we can brief execs?

Attachments: NovaOrderForm_Redlines_20261129.docx (tracked changes)

Best,
Sarah Liu
Director, Vendor Management
NovaHealth

--
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines on order form + uptime ask

Sarah —

Appreciate the thorough summary and the doc. I looped in Ben (account lead) and Laura (legal ops) to weigh in on the SLA items and to help scope tradeoffs. Initial thoughts:

- Uptime: 99.95% is a meaningful step for our shared infra; I'll need to check with infra about required capacity reservation and price impact.
- Credits: we can expand the credit tiers but would like to avoid a punitive step function that erodes the economic path for reasonable transient events.
- Response times: P1 ack at 30m is doable with a reserved escalation path on Dedicated or higher support tier; for Hosted customers this becomes a support plan add-on.
- Maintenance windows: 02:00-05:00 ET is reasonable for weekly/rolling maintenance; blackout exceptions we can take as a defined carveout with scheduled dates — we'll want a defined maximum number per year.

Laura — can you take a first pass on the redlines in the PDF? Ben — can you prepare two pricing scenarios: (A) 99.9% baseline + support add-on; (B) 99.95% baseline with a monthly commit and adjusted unit price. We'd like to give Nova a concrete tradeoff by Thursday.

I attached a copy of the MSA with our standard SLA clause for quick reference.

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_MSA_SLA_reference.pdf]

--
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines on order form + uptime ask

Rachel / Ben —

I've reviewed the tracked doc quickly and annotated two primary legal asks we should push back on:

1) The proposed credit multiplier for outages below 99.9% is overly broad. Recommend we retain a three-tier credit ladder (>=99.9% to 99.95% / 99.5% to 99.9% / <99.5%) with caps tied to monthly invoice rather than an open-ended multiplier.

2) Maintenance carveouts: we should allow for emergency maintenance without credits when safety/security patches are required; provide notice thresholds for planned vs emergency.

Suggested redline language snippets (cut-and-paste friendly):
- \"Service Credits shall not exceed 50% of the monthly recurring fees for the affected Services in any single month.\"
- \"Planned maintenance shall be scheduled with at least 48 hours' notice and will not exceed 4 hours per occurrence unless mutually agreed.\"

I'll prepare a version of the PDF with inline comments and a short memo describing rationale for tomorrow EOD. Also, Ben — please include expected price delta for 99.95% baseline vs our default.

Laura Bennett
Legal Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

--
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novahealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines on order form + uptime ask

Sarah — thanks for the clarity. Per Rachel and Laura's notes, I ran two scenarios with Finance and infra: 

Scenario A (Baseline) — 99.9% production uptime
- No change to baseline list price; Recommended support add-on to achieve 30m P1 ack (~+15% on support line item).
- Service credits: our standard three-tier ladder; monthly cap 50% of monthly fees.

Scenario B (Committed) — 99.95% production uptime with monthly commit
- Requires a 6-month minimum committed capacity (reserved pool).
- Price delta: approximately +22% on infrastructure fee line vs baseline (detailed breakdown attached).
- Credits: narrower banding with same monthly cap; we can accept a slightly higher credit % in the <99.9% band to compensate for commitment.

Attachments: pricing-scenarios_Nova_20261202.xlsx

If you can confirm which direction Nova prefers (price vs credit tradeoff) we will ready a redline-friendly order form and get legal to sign off on the specific credit caps. Happy to jump on a 30m call tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
From: Mark Hsu <mark.hsu@novahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@novahealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2026 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redlines on order form + uptime ask

Rachel / Ben / Laura —

Thanks for the fast responses and for laying out concrete options. Exec team reviewed Scenario B and they are willing to consider the 6-month commit if you can: 

- Confirm the monthly cap on credits remains 50% of monthly fees (we accept caps).
- Include explicit carveouts for scheduled blackout windows (we will provide dates falling under clinical events).
- Add a DocuSign envelope for the committed order form + MSA redline so we can push through procurement next week.

If you can send the redline-ready ORDER FORM and MSA (with tracked changes and the Scenario B pricing attached), we'll prioritize signature.

Mark Hsu
Sr. Procurement Manager
NovaHealth

Attachments in thread: NovaOrderForm_Redlines_20261129.docx, Nova_MSA_v3_track_changes.pdf, pricing-scenarios_Nova_20261202.xlsx
